subject: maths
title: Primary 6 Volume of Cubes and Cuboids
seo_title: P6 Volume of Cubes and Cuboids Worksheets: Free Primary 6 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus, PSLE)
standard_text: Finding one dimension, edge, height or face area of a cube or cuboid given its volume; use of √ and ∛
meta_desc: Free P6 volume worksheets: missing length, cube edge with ∛, water tanks in litres and PSLE-style problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Volume = length × breadth × height, so a missing length = volume ÷ (the other two lengths).
key_sub: A cube of 343 cm³ has edges of ∛343 = 7 cm, and 1 ℓ = 1000 cm³.
body_html:
Volume = length × breadth × height

Volume is the space inside a solid, in cubic units (cm³, m³). Count the 1-cm cubes in one layer, then multiply by the number of layers. That is the same as length × breadth × height.

Finding a missing length

Work backwards. Multiply the two lengths you know, then divide the volume by that answer. If you know the area of the base, height = volume ÷ area of base.

Example 1

A cuboid has a volume of 1080 cm³. It is 15 cm long and 8 cm wide. Find its height.

15 × 8 = 120 cm². Height = 1080 ÷ 120 = 9. Check: 15 × 8 × 9 = 1080.

Answer: 9 cm

Cubes: use the cube root ∛

All the edges of a cube are equal, so volume = edge × edge × edge. To find the edge, find the cube root (∛) of the volume. For a square, area = side × side, so side = √area.

Edge12345678910
Volume (edge³)1827641252163435127291000
Face area (edge²)149162536496481100

Water in tanks: 1 ℓ = 1000 cm³

The water in a tank is a cuboid too. Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank. Then change cm³ to litres by dividing by 1000.

Example 2

12 ℓ of water is poured into this tank. How much does the water level rise?

12 ℓ = 12 000 cm³. Rise = volume ÷ area of base = 12 000 ÷ (50 × 40) = 12 000 ÷ 2000.

Answer: 6 cm

Word problems: use a model

When a tank is a fraction full, draw it as equal units. Find 1 unit first.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Height = 1080 ÷ 15 (dividing by one length only)Divide by both: 1080 ÷ (15 × 8) = 9 cm
Edge of a 27 cm³ cube = 27 ÷ 3 = 9 cmUse the cube root: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, so 3 cm
60 000 cm³ = 60 000 ℓDivide by 1000: 60 000 cm³ = 60 ℓ
Using the height of the tank for the waterUse the depth of the water
Writing cm² for a volumeArea is cm², volume is cm³

faq.q: What is taught about volume in P6 maths?
faq.a: Primary 6 students find a missing length, breadth or height of a cuboid from its volume, find the edge of a cube with ∛, and solve water-tank problems using 1 ℓ = 1000 cm³. These are part of Area and Volume in the MOE syllabus.

faq.q: How do I find the height of a cuboid from its volume?
faq.a: Divide the volume by the area of the base (length × breadth). For 1080 cm³ with a base of 15 cm by 8 cm, the height is 1080 ÷ 120 = 9 cm.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with volume of cubes?
faq.a: Dividing the volume by 3 instead of finding the cube root. A cube of 27 cm³ has edges of 3 cm, because 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, not 27 ÷ 3 = 9 cm.

faq.q: Are water tank questions in the PSLE?
faq.a: Yes. PSLE Paper 2 often has multi-step tank questions about water poured in or out and the change in water level. Students need 1 ℓ = 1000 cm³ and depth = volume ÷ area of base.

items.q: The solid is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: One layer has 2 rows of 4 cubes = 8 cubes. There are 3 layers: 8 × 3 = 24 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too (only 18 cubes can be seen).

items.q: The solid is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: One layer has 3 rows of 3 cubes = 9 cubes. There are 2 layers: 9 × 2 = 18 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too (only 14 cubes can be seen).

items.q: The solid is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: One layer has 2 rows of 5 cubes = 10 cubes. There are 2 layers: 10 × 2 = 20 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too (only 16 cubes can be seen).

items.q: The solid is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: One layer has 3 rows of 4 cubes = 12 cubes. There are 3 layers: 12 × 3 = 36 cm³. Count the hidden cubes too (only 24 cubes can be seen).

items.q: Find the volume of the cuboid.
items.e: Volume = length × breadth × height = 10 × 6 × 9 = 60 × 9 = 540 cm³. Multiply all three lengths and write the answer in cubic units (cm³).

items.q: Find the volume of the cuboid.
items.e: Volume = length × breadth × height = 7 × 4 × 6 = 28 × 6 = 168 cm³. Multiply all three lengths and write the answer in cubic units (cm³).

items.q: Find the volume of the cuboid.
items.e: Volume = length × breadth × height = 9 × 3 × 7 = 27 × 7 = 189 m³. Multiply all three lengths and write the answer in cubic units (m³).

items.q: Find the volume of the cuboid.
items.e: Volume = length × breadth × height = 12 × 8 × 10 = 96 × 10 = 960 cm³. Multiply all three lengths and write the answer in cubic units (cm³).

items.q: Find the volume of the cuboid.
items.e: Volume = length × breadth × height = 11 × 7 × 12 = 77 × 12 = 924 cm³. Multiply all three lengths and write the answer in cubic units (cm³).

items.q: Find the volume of the cuboid.
items.e: Volume = length × breadth × height = 12 × 4 × 10 = 48 × 10 = 480 m³. Multiply all three lengths and write the answer in cubic units (m³).

items.q: Find the volume of the cuboid.
items.e: Volume = length × breadth × height = 16 × 6 × 11 = 96 × 11 = 1056 cm³. Multiply all three lengths and write the answer in cubic units (cm³).

items.q: A cube has edges of 5 cm. Find its volume.
items.e: All the edges of a cube are equal: volume = 5 × 5 × 5 = 25 × 5 = 125 cm³.

items.q: A cube has edges of 8 cm. Find its volume.
items.e: All the edges of a cube are equal: volume = 8 × 8 × 8 = 64 × 8 = 512 cm³.

items.q: A cube has edges of 12 m. Find its volume.
items.e: All the edges of a cube are equal: volume = 12 × 12 × 12 = 144 × 12 = 1728 m³.

items.q: A cuboid is 2.5 m long, 1.2 m wide and 0.8 m high. Find its volume.
A block of wood is 1.5 m long, 0.6 m wide and 2 m tall. Find its volume.
items.e: Volume = 1.5 × 0.6 × 2 = 0.9 × 2 = 1.8 m³. 0.9 m² is only the area of the base.

items.q: A container has a capacity of 4500 cm³. What is its capacity in litres? (1 ℓ = 1000 cm³)
A jug holds 2 ℓ 350 ml of water. What is this volume in cm³?
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1000 cm³ and 1 ml = 1 cm³. 2 ℓ 350 ml = 2000 ml + 350 ml = 2350 ml = 2350 cm³.

items.q: How many cubic centimetres are there in 1 m³?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so a 1 m cube is 100 cm × 100 cm × 100 cm = 1 000 000 cm³. (1 m² = 10 000 cm², because area has only two lengths.)

items.q: Which of these is a volume?
items.e: Volume is measured in cubic units (cm³, m³). cm² is an area, cm is a length and kg is a mass.

items.q: The volume of the cuboid is 715 cm³. Find the unknown height.
items.e: 13 × 5 × ? = 715, so 65 × ? = 715. ? = 715 ÷ 65 = 11 cm. Divide by both of the other lengths. Check: 13 × 5 × 11 = 715.

items.q: The volume of the cuboid is 308 cm³. Find the unknown breadth.
items.e: 7 × 11 × ? = 308, so 77 × ? = 308. ? = 308 ÷ 77 = 4 cm. Divide by both of the other lengths. Check: 7 × 4 × 11 = 308.

items.q: The volume of the cuboid is 270 m³. Find the unknown length.
items.e: 3 × 10 × ? = 270, so 30 × ? = 270. ? = 270 ÷ 30 = 9 m. Divide by both of the other lengths. Check: 9 × 3 × 10 = 270.

items.q: The volume of the cuboid is 288 cm³. Find the unknown height.
items.e: 8 × 4 × ? = 288, so 32 × ? = 288. ? = 288 ÷ 32 = 9 cm. Divide by both of the other lengths. Check: 8 × 4 × 9 = 288.

items.q: A cuboid has a volume of 1080 cm³. Its length is 15 cm and its breadth is 8 cm. Find its height.
A cuboid has a volume of 840 cm³. Its length is 12 cm and its height is 10 cm. Find its breadth.
A cuboid has a volume of 600 cm³. Its breadth is 6 cm and its height is 5 cm. Find its length.
A cuboid has a volume of 2100 cm³. Its length is 25 cm and its breadth is 14 cm. Find its height.
A cuboid has a volume of 2160 cm³. Its length is 18 cm and its height is 8 cm. Find its breadth.
A cuboid has a volume of 1728 cm³. Its breadth is 9 cm and its height is 12 cm. Find its length.
A cuboid has a square base of side 5 cm. Its volume is 200 cm³. Find its height.
items.e: Area of base = 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Height = 200 ÷ 25 = 8 cm. (5 × 2 = 10 is not the area of the base.)

items.q: A cuboid has a square base of side 6 cm. Its volume is 252 cm³. Find its height.
items.e: Area of base = 6 × 6 = 36 cm². Height = 252 ÷ 36 = 7 cm. (6 × 2 = 12 is not the area of the base.)

items.q: A cuboid has a square base of side 9 cm. Its volume is 324 cm³. Find its height.
items.e: Area of base = 9 × 9 = 81 cm². Height = 324 ÷ 81 = 4 cm. (9 × 2 = 18 is not the area of the base.)

items.q: A cuboid has a volume of 400 cm³. The area of its base is 80 cm². Find its height.
items.e: Volume = area of base × height, so height = volume ÷ area of base = 400 ÷ 80 = 5 cm. Check: 80 × 5 = 400.

items.q: A cuboid has a volume of 960 cm³. The area of its base is 120 cm². Find its height.
items.e: Volume = area of base × height, so height = volume ÷ area of base = 960 ÷ 120 = 8 cm. Check: 120 × 8 = 960.

items.q: A cuboid has a volume of 1000 cm³. The area of its base is 250 cm². Find its height.
items.e: Volume = area of base × height, so height = volume ÷ area of base = 1000 ÷ 250 = 4 cm. Check: 250 × 4 = 1000.

items.q: A cuboid has a volume of 360 cm³ and a height of 6 cm. Find the area of its base.
items.e: Area of base = volume ÷ height = 360 ÷ 6 = 60 cm². An area is in square units (cm²).

items.q: A cuboid has a volume of 1350 cm³ and a height of 9 cm. Find the area of its base.
items.e: Area of base = volume ÷ height = 1350 ÷ 9 = 150 cm². An area is in square units (cm²).

items.q: A container has a volume of 1.2 m³. It is 2 m long and 0.5 m high. Find its breadth.
A concrete block has a volume of 4.8 m³. Its base is 2.4 m by 1.25 m. Find its height.
items.e: Area of base = 2.4 × 1.25 = 3 m². Height = 4.8 ÷ 3 = 1.6 m. Check: 3 × 1.6 = 4.8 m³.

items.q: The volume of this cube is 512 cm³. Find the length of one edge.
items.e: Edge × edge × edge = 512. Find the number that multiplies by itself 3 times to give 512: 8 × 8 × 8 = 512, so ∛512 = 8 cm.

items.q: The volume of this cube is 64 cm³. Find the length of one edge.
items.e: Edge × edge × edge = 64. Find the number that multiplies by itself 3 times to give 64: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, so ∛64 = 4 cm.

items.q: The volume of this cube is 1000 cm³. Find the length of one edge.
items.e: Edge × edge × edge = 1000. Find the number that multiplies by itself 3 times to give 1000: 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000, so ∛1000 = 10 cm.

items.q: The volume of this cube is 343 m³. Find the length of one edge.
items.e: Edge × edge × edge = 343. Find the number that multiplies by itself 3 times to give 343: 7 × 7 × 7 = 343, so ∛343 = 7 m.

items.q: A cube has a volume of 125 cm³. What is the length of each edge?
items.e: Edge × edge × edge = 125. Find the number that multiplies by itself 3 times to give 125: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125, so ∛125 = 5 cm.

items.q: A cube has a volume of 729 cm³. What is the length of each edge?
items.e: Edge × edge × edge = 729. Find the number that multiplies by itself 3 times to give 729: 9 × 9 × 9 = 729, so ∛729 = 9 cm. Do not divide by 3: 729 ÷ 3 = 243, and 243 × 243 × 243 is not 729.

items.q: A cube has a volume of 216 m³. What is the length of each edge?
items.e: Edge × edge × edge = 216. Find the number that multiplies by itself 3 times to give 216: 6 × 6 × 6 = 216, so ∛216 = 6 m. Do not divide by 3: 216 ÷ 3 = 72, and 72 × 72 × 72 is not 216.

items.q: A cube has a volume of 27 cm³. What is the length of each edge?
items.e: Edge × edge × edge = 27. Find the number that multiplies by itself 3 times to give 27: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, so ∛27 = 3 cm. Do not divide by 3: 27 ÷ 3 = 9, and 9 × 9 × 9 is not 27.

items.q: A square has an area of 49 cm². Find the length of one side.
items.e: Side × side = 49. 7 × 7 = 49, so √49 = 7 cm. Do not halve the area or divide it by 4 (÷ 4 finds the side from the perimeter).

items.q: A square has an area of 81 m². Find the length of one side.
items.e: Side × side = 81. 9 × 9 = 81, so √81 = 9 m. Do not halve the area or divide it by 4 (÷ 4 finds the side from the perimeter).

items.q: A square has an area of 121 cm². Find the length of one side.
items.e: Side × side = 121. 11 × 11 = 121, so √121 = 11 cm. Do not halve the area or divide it by 4 (÷ 4 finds the side from the perimeter).

items.q: A square has an area of 144 cm². Find the length of one side.
items.e: Side × side = 144. 12 × 12 = 144, so √144 = 12 cm. Do not halve the area or divide it by 4 (÷ 4 finds the side from the perimeter).

items.q: A cube has a volume of 64 cm³. Find the area of one face.
items.e: Edge = ∛64 = 4 cm. A face is a 4 cm by 4 cm square: 4 × 4 = 16 cm². (All 6 faces would be 96 cm².)

items.q: A cube has a volume of 343 cm³. Find the area of one face.
items.e: Edge = ∛343 = 7 cm. A face is a 7 cm by 7 cm square: 7 × 7 = 49 cm². (All 6 faces would be 294 cm².)

items.q: A cube has a volume of 1000 cm³. Find the area of one face.
items.e: Edge = ∛1000 = 10 cm. A face is a 10 cm by 10 cm square: 10 × 10 = 100 cm². (All 6 faces would be 600 cm².)

items.q: A cube has a volume of 729 cm³. Find the area of one face.
items.e: Edge = ∛729 = 9 cm. A face is a 9 cm by 9 cm square: 9 × 9 = 81 cm². (All 6 faces would be 486 cm².)

items.q: One face of a cube has an area of 49 cm². Find the volume of the cube.
One face of a cube has an area of 81 cm². Find the volume of the cube.
The total length of all the edges of a cube is 96 cm. Find the volume of the cube.
items.e: A cube has 12 equal edges (not 4 or 6). Edge = 96 ÷ 12 = 8 cm. Volume = 8 × 8 × 8 = 512 cm³.

items.q: A cuboid has a square base and a height of 5 cm. Its volume is 245 cm³. Find the length of one side of its base.
items.e: Area of base = 245 ÷ 5 = 49 cm². The base is a square, so its side = √49 = 7 cm.

items.q: How many litres of water can this tank hold?
A tank is 60 cm long, 45 cm wide and 40 cm high. How many litres of water can it hold?
A tank is 80 cm long, 50 cm wide and 45 cm high. How many litres of water can it hold?
The water in the tank is 20 cm deep. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 40 × 30 × 20 = 24 000 cm³ = 24 ℓ (÷ 1000).

items.q: The water in the tank is 35 cm deep. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 60 × 40 × 35 = 84 000 cm³ = 84 ℓ (÷ 1000).

items.q: The water in the tank is 28 cm deep. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 50 × 25 × 28 = 35 000 cm³ = 35 ℓ (÷ 1000).

items.q: 30 ℓ of water is poured into an empty tank. The tank is 40 cm long, 25 cm wide and 45 cm high. What is the depth of the water?
24 ℓ of water is poured into this empty tank. What is the depth of the water?
36 ℓ of water is poured into an empty tank. The tank is 60 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm high. What is the depth of the water?
A tank has a base 50 cm by 40 cm. 12 ℓ of water is poured into it. By how much does the water level rise?
Ali pours 27 ℓ more water into the tank. What is the new depth of the water?
A tank has a base 30 cm by 20 cm. It contains water 8 cm deep. 4.2 ℓ of water is added. What is the new depth of the water?
A tank has a base 60 cm by 30 cm. The water in it is 40 cm deep. 27 ℓ of water is drained out. What is the depth of the water now?
Water is let out until the water is 20 cm deep. How many litres of water were let out?
items.e: The water fell by 32 − 20 = 12 cm. Volume let out = 50 × 40 × 12 = 24 000 cm³ = 24 ℓ.

items.q: A tank has a base 80 cm by 50 cm. The water in it is 45 cm deep. 60 ℓ of water is used. What is the depth of the water now?
How many more litres of water are needed to fill the tank to the brim?
items.e: Empty part: 60 − 35 = 25 cm high. 50 × 40 × 25 = 50 000 cm³ = 50 ℓ.

items.q: A tank 40 cm long, 40 cm wide and 50 cm high contains 32 ℓ of water. How many more litres are needed to fill it completely?
items.e: Capacity = 40 × 40 × 50 = 80 000 cm³ = 80 ℓ. More water needed = 80 − 32 = 48 ℓ.

items.q: A tank 60 cm long, 30 cm wide and 45 cm high is empty. Water is poured in until it is 30 cm deep. How many more litres are needed to fill it to the brim?
items.e: The empty part is 45 − 30 = 15 cm high. 60 × 30 × 15 = 27 000 cm³ = 27 ℓ.

items.q: A tank is 60 cm long, 50 cm wide and 40 cm high. It is 34 full of water. How many litres of water are in it?
items.e: Capacity = 60 × 50 × 40 = 120 000 cm³ = 120 ℓ. 34 of 120 ℓ = 90 ℓ.

items.q: A tank is 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 60 cm high. It is 25 full of water. What is the depth of the water?
items.e: The water fills 25 of the height: 25 × 60 = 24 cm. The length and breadth do not change.

items.q: Kavya fills Tank A, 40 cm by 30 cm by 25 cm, to the brim with water. She then pours all the water into an empty Tank B with a base 50 cm by 40 cm. What is the depth of the water in Tank B?
items.e: Water in A = 40 × 30 × 25 = 30 000 cm³. Depth in B = 30 000 ÷ (50 × 40) = 30 000 ÷ 2000 = 15 cm. The water is the same; only the base changes.

items.q: Mrs Lim's tank is 35 full. It has 36 ℓ of water in it. How many more litres of water are needed to fill the tank?
items.e: 3 units = 36 ℓ, so 1 unit = 12 ℓ. The empty part is 2 units = 2 × 12 = 24 ℓ. (The full tank is 5 units = 60 ℓ.)

items.q: A tank is 25 full of water. After 18 ℓ of water is added, it is 45 full. What is the capacity of the tank?
items.e: The 18 ℓ fills 45 − 25 = 25 of the tank. 2 units = 18 ℓ, so 1 unit = 9 ℓ. Capacity = 5 units = 5 × 9 = 45 ℓ.

items.q: Container A has 3 times as much water as Container B. Together they hold 48 ℓ. Jun Jie pours water from A into B until they have the same amount. How many litres does he pour?
items.e: 4 units = 48 ℓ, so 1 unit = 12 ℓ. A has 36 ℓ and B has 12 ℓ. Each needs 48 ÷ 2 = 24 ℓ, so pour 36 − 24 = 12 ℓ (1 unit).

items.q: An empty tank is 60 cm long, 40 cm wide and 50 cm high. A tap fills it at 8 ℓ per minute. How long does it take to fill the tank?
A tank 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 45 cm high has water 15 cm deep. Water flows in from a tap at 6 ℓ per minute. How long will it take to fill the tank to the brim?
items.e: The empty part is 45 − 15 = 30 cm high: 50 × 40 × 30 = 60 000 cm³ = 60 ℓ. Time = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 min. (15 min would fill the whole tank, 90 ℓ.)

items.q: Sarah packs 3-cm cubes into a box 12 cm long, 9 cm wide and 6 cm high. How many cubes fit in the box?
items.e: Along the length: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Breadth: 9 ÷ 3 = 3. Height: 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Cubes = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24. Or: the box is 648 cm³ and one cube is 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cm³, so 648 ÷ 27 = 24. (648 ÷ 3 = 216 divides by the edge, not the volume of a cube.)

items.q: A tank has a base 30 cm by 20 cm and contains some water. Ali puts a stone into it. The stone sinks and the water level rises by 2 cm. Find the volume of the stone.
items.e: The stone pushes up a layer of water 30 cm by 20 cm by 2 cm. Volume of stone = 30 × 20 × 2 = 1200 cm³.

items.q: Tank A has a base 40 cm by 25 cm and water 30 cm deep. Tank B has a base 50 cm by 30 cm and is empty. Water is poured from A into B until the water in both tanks is the same depth. What is this depth?
items.e: Water = 40 × 25 × 30 = 30 000 cm³. The two bases together are 1000 + 1500 = 2500 cm². Depth = 30 000 ÷ 2500 = 12 cm. (15 cm is half of 30, but the bases are not the same size.)

items.q: Ethan has a block of clay 20 cm by 12 cm by 8 cm. He cuts it into cubes with 4-cm edges. How many cubes does he make?
items.e: Clay = 20 × 12 × 8 = 1920 cm³. One cube = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 cm³. 1920 ÷ 64 = 30 cubes. Check: 20 ÷ 4 = 5, 12 ÷ 4 = 3, 8 ÷ 4 = 2, and 5 × 3 × 2 = 30. (1920 ÷ 4 = 480 uses the edge, not the volume of a cube.)

items.q: A wooden cube has a volume of 512 cm³. Ribbon is glued along every edge. How much ribbon is used?
items.e: Edge = ∛512 = 8 cm. A cube has 12 edges: 12 × 8 = 96 cm.

items.q: A box has a square base. Its height is 15 cm and its volume is 960 cm³. Find the length of one side of the base.
items.e: Area of base = 960 ÷ 15 = 64 cm². The base is a square: side = √64 = 8 cm.

items.q: A tank 80 cm long and 50 cm wide has water 45 cm deep. Water drains out at 12 ℓ per minute. How long does it take for the depth to fall to 15 cm?
items.e: The depth falls by 45 − 15 = 30 cm. Water drained = 80 × 50 × 30 = 120 000 cm³ = 120 ℓ. Time = 120 ÷ 12 = 10 min. (15 min would empty the whole 180 ℓ.)

items.q: Mr Rahman's tank has a base 60 cm by 40 cm and holds 72 ℓ of water. He uses 13 of the water, then 14 of the remaining water. What is the depth of the water left?
items.e: 13 of 72 = 24 ℓ, leaving 48 ℓ. 14 of 48 = 12 ℓ, leaving 36 ℓ. 36 ℓ = 36 000 cm³. Depth = 36 000 ÷ (60 × 40) = 36 000 ÷ 2400 = 15 cm. (Take 14 of the remaining 48 ℓ, not of 72 ℓ.)

items.q: A fish tank is 40 cm long, 40 cm wide and 50 cm high. It is filled to 75% of its height. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Depth = 75% of 50 = 37.5 cm. Water = 40 × 40 × 37.5 = 60 000 cm³ = 60 ℓ. (Or 75% of the 80 ℓ capacity = 60 ℓ.)

items.q: The volumes of water in Containers P and Q are in the ratio 2 : 3. P has 6 ℓ less water than Q. How much water is in Q?
items.e: Q has 1 unit more than P. 1 unit = 6 ℓ. Q = 3 units = 3 × 6 = 18 ℓ. (P has 12 ℓ; together 30 ℓ.)

items.q: Zhi Hao pours 4 jugs of water into an empty tank with a base 50 cm by 20 cm. Each jug holds 1 ℓ 250 ml. What is the depth of the water in the tank?
A tank 60 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high is full of water. Devi fills 18 bottles of 1.5 ℓ each from the tank. What is the depth of the water left in the tank?
Cube A has edges of 6 cm. The volume of Cube B is 8 times the volume of Cube A. Find the length of an edge of Cube B.
items.e: Volume of A = 6 × 6 × 6 = 216 cm³. Volume of B = 8 × 216 = 1728 cm³. 12 × 12 × 12 = 1728, so the edge is 12 cm. (8 times the volume does not mean 8 times the edge.)

items.q: A metal cube with edges of 12 cm is put into this tank. The cube sinks to the bottom. What is the new depth of the water?
items.e: Volume of cube = 12 × 12 × 12 = 1728 cm³ (the cube is under the water, since 12 cm < 18 cm). Rise = 1728 ÷ (40 × 30) = 1728 ÷ 1200 = 1.44 cm. The water goes up, so new depth = 18 + 1.44 = 19.44 cm.
